business_problem: APR Kerbside sought to identify and sort used Tetra Pak beverage cartons from kerbside recycling, helping divert more valuable resources from landfill.
solution_summary: APR Kerbside installed and commissioned an AI-powered robot at its Material Recovery Facility (MRF) in Truganina, Victoria, to identify and sort used Tetra Pak beverage cartons from the kerbside recycling stream. The incoming stream comes from residents’ yellow-lidded bins and includes paper and cardboard, steel, aluminium, plastics, and cartons. Before final deployment, the robot was being trained to recognize carton types including milk, soy, oat, almond, stock, and juice; the source does not identify the robot maker, model, sensors, software, data store, or operating interfaces. APR planned to transport recovered cartons to saveBOARD’s facility in Warragamba, New South Wales, for recycling into building materials, pending a Victoria saveBOARD plant. Tetra Pak and APR jointly funded the installation. Further MRF expansion and additional robots are described only as future plans.

evidence_quotes: A robot that uses artificial intelligence to sort used Tetra Pak beverage cartons has been installed at APR Kerbside’s Material Recovery Facility (MRF) in Truganina, Victoria.
The robot has been training, learning to recognise all the different types of beverage cartons.
This glass-out facility has the capacity to process up to 20,000 tonnes of materials annually.
APR Kerbside plans to transport Tetra Pak beverage cartons to the newly opened saveBOARD facility in Warragamba NSW so they can be recycled into sustainable building materials.
